newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks open lower as yen, Dow hit exporters.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks open lower as yen, Dow hit exporters.

text.p: Tokyo stocks dropped at the opening on Monday, as leading export-driven shares were hit by the yen's climb against the dollar and Wall Street stocks' tumble on Friday, brokers said.
By 0006 GMT, the 225-share Nikkei average had lost 248.62 points or 1.27 percent to trade at 19,355.84. September Nikkei futures were ask-only at 19,500 against their Friday close at 19,680.
Brokers said that, if the benchmark Nikkei index breaches 19,233, a low hit last week, the next support level would be the psychologically important 19,000 mark.
On Friday in New York, the Dow industrials slid 156.78 points to end at 8,031.22. It was the ninth-largest point decline in a single session in the blue-chip average's history.
The dollar was quoted around 115.50 yen in early Asia trade on Monday, against 118.42/52 yen in late Tokyo trade on Friday and New York's Friday close of 114.75/85.
